Wraparound Care: ABC Sports Stars
We are proud to offer wraparound care with ABC Sports Stars Ltd. The breakfast club runs from 7.30am and the afterschool club runs until 6pm.
To book your child a place, please visit: https://abcsportsstars.ipalbookings.com/
Wraparound Care: ABC Sports Stars
A message from ABC Sports Stars
"Founded in 2021, ABC Sports Stars is a unique youth sports club, here to help children of all ages get active and have fun outdoors. Based in Lewisham we work with schools, nurseries and activity centres throughout the South London area.
All members of our tram are fully DBS checked, holding both the latest safeguarding training and paediatric first aid. We are committed to the safety of everyone who takes part. We hold qualifications in PE (Level 3) and youth football (Level 2 Youth Module, FA Football). Some of our team have previously been working in nurseries and other childcare environments, whilst some are studying for teaching degrees."
- Jake Hattam, Managing Director
"We believe we bring a fresh energetic outlook to wraparound care, getting children ready for their school day and activities to participate in afterschool, whilst in safe space and all at a reasonable cost."
- Mark Upton, Company Secretary

pageCache.text:
Expressive Art and Design
Expressive Arts and Design (EAD) is a specific area of the EYFS curriculum. One of the ideas behind EAD is that the quality and variety of what children see, hear and participate in is crucial for developing their understanding, self-expression, vocabulary and ability to communicate through the arts. The frequency, repetition and depth of their experiences are fundamental to their progress in interpreting and appreciating what they hear, respond to and observe.
EAD encompasses a wide breadth of creative areas, such as listening and responding to music, singing, dancing and performing, experimenting with colour mixing and different textures, creating models (for example, junk modelling), small world play, building and construction, and role-play activities.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome | St Saviour's Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
A Welcome from Our Head Teacher
Thank you for visiting the St Saviour’s website. I hope that, as you look around, you get a real sense of what makes our school such a special place.
It is a real privilege to be the Head Teacher of St Saviour’s. We are a school built on high expectations, nurture and genuine care. Our children are curious, friendly and enthusiastic and our staff are dedicated and committed. There is a wonderful sense of community that runs throughout the school, bringing together our pupils, staff, families, governors and the wider community.
For me, education is about giving every child the opportunity to flourish. We have high standards and high expectations, and we want our children to enjoy a rich and ambitious curriculum that inspires them to learn, encourages them to ask questions and helps them to make sense of the world around them.
Our curriculum is designed to give children both the knowledge and the skills they need to thrive. We want learning to be meaningful, engaging and memorable, with opportunities for children to explore their interests, develop their talents and make connections between different areas of learning. We value creativity, curiosity and a love of learning, and we want our children to leave us with not only a strong foundation of knowledge, but also the confidence and independence to keep learning throughout their lives.
We believe that children learn best when they feel safe, happy and valued. That is why nurture and care are at the heart of our school. We want every child to feel that they belong here, that they are known and cared for, and that they can be themselves.
Our school values are rooted in the Fruits of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. These are not simply words on a page, they are values that we strive to live by every day in our classrooms, in the playground and in the way we treat one another as a school community.
Every child is unique, and we want them to be proud of who they are, feel confident in their own abilities and always willing to have a go, even when something feels difficult. We encourage our children to see mistakes as part of learning and to approach new challenges with confidence and resilience.
Whether you are a prospective family thinking about joining St Saviour’s, a current parent or carer, or simply finding out a little more about our school, I hope our website gives you a genuine feel for who we are and what we stand for.
If you would like to find out more or arrange a visit, please do get in touch. We would be delighted to welcome you to St Saviour’s and show you our school for yourself.
With very best wishes,
ST SAVIOUR'S CHURCH WELCOMES YOU TOO!

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths | St Saviour's Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Maths
The statutory framework for the EYFS states that during the early years, children need to 'develop a strong grounding in number' in order for children to develop the 'building blocks' needed for them to 'excel mathematically'.
The statutory framework discusses that children should be able to count confidently and develop a deep understanding of the numbers to 10. Children receive lots of opportunities to build up their knowledge and apply what they have learned using manipulatives, such as 'pebbles and tens frames for organising counting'. It is through a variety of frequent opportunities that children increase their knowledge and are able to build a mastery of mathematics.
We also support children to develop a positive attitude and model how to look for patterns and spot connections. It is also essential that children are encouraged to 'have a go', talk to adults and their peers about the things they notice, and are not concerned about making mistakes.

Oak Class

How parents/carers can support their child's learning in maths:
Encourage children to use Mathletics at home - it's a fantastic (and free!) resource that helps to consolidate learning.
Each child has a login (found in Reading Record) and should complete 2x set assignments each week.
Times Tables Rockstars:-
By the end of Year 4, children should be fluent in their 1x-12x times tables. To strengthen your child's arithmetic skills, please encourage regular practice as the Year 4 children will be completing their Multiplication check at the end of this year. They can access Times Tables Rockstars, another brilliant site with a fun and fast paced approach to times tables. Individual logins can be found in Reading Records.
Every Friday we complete a multiplication test (popcorn test) in class. Your child will receive a copy of this for optional (but recommended) further practice.

Maths
In Maths this term, we are looking at money and multiplication
Children
Maple Class
The core learning objectives that we'll exploring this term include:
Knowing that money represents value
Understanding that multiplication means “groups of” or repeated addition
Explaining answers using simple language (e.g. “I have 3 groups of 2”
Working out how to pay for items
Finding different ways to make the same amount of money
Solving real-life multiplication problems (e.g. “2 bags with 5 apples in each”)
